questions.q: According to the European Commission, who does corporate sustainability reporting help?
options: Investors, civil society organisations, consumers and other stakeholders evaluating companies' sustainability performance
questions.explain: Comparable, reliable disclosures let stakeholders judge sustainability performance.
questions.evidence: This helps investors, civil society organisations, consumers and other stakeholders to evaluate the sustainability performance of companies

questions.q: Companies subject to the CSRD must report according to which standards?
questions.explain: The ESRS set out what and how companies disclose under the CSRD.
questions.evidence: Companies subject to the CSRD have to report according to European Sustainability Reporting Standards (ESRS).

questions.q: What is the EU taxonomy for sustainable activities?
options: A ranking of the greenest countries
A classification system defining criteria for economic activities aligned with net zero by 2050 and wider environmental goals
questions.explain: It is a transparency tool that directs investment to activities needed for the transition.
questions.evidence: The taxonomy is a classification system that defines criteria for economic activities that are aligned with a net zero trajectory by 2050 and the broader environmental goals other than climate.

questions.q: UK SRS S1 and UK SRS S2 are UK versions of which standards?
questions.explain: They are endorsed versions of the ISSB's IFRS Sustainability Disclosure Standards.
questions.evidence: The UK government consulted on the exposure drafts of the UK versions of IFRS S1 and IFRS S2 – respectively called UK SRS S1 and UK SRS S2.

questions.q: What role was the International Sustainability Standards Board (ISSB) created for?
options: To create a global baseline for sustainability reporting
questions.explain: It was announced at COP26 in Glasgow in 2021.
questions.evidence: with the role of creating a global baseline for sustainability reporting.

questions.q: Which standard does the SECR worked example use to calculate emissions?
options: The GHG Reporting Protocol – Corporate Standard
A standard invented by each trust
questions.explain: Several independent standards are recognised; the example uses the GHG Protocol.
questions.evidence: the standard used in the worked example set out below is the GHG Reporting Protocol - Corporate Standard

questions.q: Are organisations expected to hire specialist consultants to meet the SECR requirements in the example guidance?
options: Only if they have more than one building
No — it is not expected; the figures can be calculated in-house
questions.explain: The worked example shows how to calculate the figures yourself.
questions.evidence: It is not expected that academy trusts will need to engage specialist consultants to support the reporting requirements

questions.q: What is the aim of England's resources and waste strategy?
options: To become a world leader in using resources efficiently and reducing the amount of waste created
questions.explain: It favours recovering and regenerating products and materials.
questions.evidence: Our plan is to become a world leader in using resources efficiently and reducing the amount of waste we create as a society.

questions.q: What do the UK Greening Government Commitments require for information technology?
options: That all IT is bought from UK suppliers
That servers run only at night
That government reduces the carbon emissions and waste caused by its IT
questions.explain: Digital services have an environmental footprint that must be reduced.
questions.evidence: The Greening Government Commitments require government to reduce the carbon (CO2) emissions and waste caused by its information technology

questions.q: What does environmental sustainability mean in the Data and AI Ethics Framework?
options: Thinking about the wider impact of your project on people and the planet, and being mindful of the resources you use
questions.explain: Consider it from the start — it shapes choices of tools, suppliers and infrastructure.
questions.evidence: Environmental sustainability means thinking about the wider impact of your project on people and the planet, and being mindful about the resources you use every day.

questions.q: When do the first companies under the CSRD have to apply the new rules?
options: For the 2024 financial year, in reports published in 2025
questions.explain: More companies come into scope in later years.
questions.evidence: have to apply the new rules for the first time in the 2024 financial year, for reports published in 2025

questions.q: Who develops the draft European Sustainability Reporting Standards?
options: EFRAG, an independent body bringing together various stakeholders
questions.explain: EFRAG was previously known as the European Financial Reporting Advisory Group.
questions.evidence: The standards are developed in a draft form by the EFRAG

questions.q: What role does the EU taxonomy play in sustainable finance?
options: It bans investment in all industry
It helps direct investment to the activities most needed for the transition
questions.explain: It supports the European Green Deal objectives.
questions.evidence: It helps direct investments to the economic activities most needed for the transition

questions.q: Why is a common classification of sustainable activities needed?
options: To give everyone a common language and a clear definition of 'sustainable'
To let each company define sustainability its own way
questions.explain: Without shared definitions, 'green' claims can't be compared.
questions.evidence: a common language and a clear definition of what is ‘sustainable’ is needed

questions.q: Taxonomy-aligned activities are consistent with which trajectory?
questions.explain: Criteria also cover environmental goals other than climate.
questions.evidence: aligned with a net zero trajectory by 2050

questions.q: The EU taxonomy is described as a cornerstone of what?
questions.explain: It is also an important market transparency tool.
questions.evidence: The EU taxonomy is a cornerstone of the EU’s sustainable finance framework

questions.q: Where are the main financial reporting requirements for academy trusts set out?
questions.explain: The SECR guidance supplements, but does not replace, those requirements.
questions.evidence: The main financial reporting requirements for academy trusts are set out in the Academies Accounts Direction

questions.q: What does 'gas combustion' include for SECR reporting?
options: Gas used for stationary or mobile activities the trust is responsible for
Gas used by staff at home
questions.explain: Responsibility, not location, decides what is included.
questions.evidence: includes gas consumed for stationary or mobile activities for which the academy trust is responsible

questions.q: If some required information is missing, what should the trust report?
options: That it is missing, what is omitted and how it will get it in future
questions.explain: Transparency about gaps is better than silence.
questions.evidence: this fact should be reported, and the academy trust should explain what is omitted and what steps it is taking to acquire this information in future

questions.q: In the worked example, how did the trust record mini-bus and business travel?
options: As the number of miles travelled during the year
questions.explain: Mileage is then converted to emissions with conversion factors.
questions.evidence: For the mini-buses and business travel, the trust has recorded the number of miles travelled during the year.

questions.q: In the worked example, how are the trust's academies heated?
options: Each has its own gas-fuelled boilers
questions.explain: Gas use and purchased electricity are the main energy sources.
questions.evidence: The academy trust has 3 academies, all with their own boilers which are gas fuelled and electricity is purchased.

questions.q: What does England's resources and waste strategy aim to make the country a world leader in?
options: Using resources efficiently and reducing waste
questions.explain: It is part of the 25 Year Environment Plan.
questions.evidence: Our plan is to become a world leader in using resources efficiently and reducing the amount of waste we create as a society.

questions.q: What does the strategy say about products and materials at the end of use?
options: Recover and regenerate them whenever possible
Export them for others to handle
questions.explain: Regeneration gives materials a new lease of life.
questions.evidence: We should recover and regenerate products and materials whenever we can, giving them a new lease of life.

questions.q: How does the strategy want to help consumers with the materials in products?
options: To recycle them and dispose of them in the most environmentally sensitive ways
questions.explain: Clear information helps people make the right choice.
questions.evidence: We want to help consumers to be able to recycle the materials they contain and dispose of them in the most environmentally sensitive ways.

questions.q: Which team can government projects contact for sustainable technology advice?
questions.explain: STAR stands for Sustainable Technology Advice & Reporting.
questions.evidence: you can contact the cross-government Sustainable Technology Advice & Reporting (STAR) team

questions.q: At the start of a technology project, which question should you consider?
options: What are your organisation's sustainability goals?
questions.explain: Project objectives can then support those goals.
questions.evidence: you should consider these questions: What are your organisation’s sustainability goals?

questions.q: What does developing and training AI models, especially LLMs, require?
options: Critical minerals, energy, water and computing resources
questions.explain: That footprint is why sustainability belongs in AI project design.
questions.evidence: requires the use of critical minerals, energy, water and computing resources

questions.q: How can data and AI support environmental goals?
options: By ending the need for regulation
For example by predicting weather or monitoring biodiversity
questions.explain: AI can help the environment while also having its own footprint.
questions.evidence: Data and AI can support environmental goals, such as predicting weather patterns or monitoring biodiversity levels.

questions.q: What helps make sustainability a core part of project design?
options: Clear sustainability objectives and greener software practices
questions.explain: Objectives make sustainability measurable from the start.
questions.evidence: Setting clear sustainability objectives and using greener software practices will help make sustainability a core part of your project design.

questions.q: Beyond the environment, what else does sustainability cover in how technology is made and used?
questions.explain: This applies from design and manufacture to use and disposal.
questions.evidence: This means supporting inclusion, fairness and human rights in how technologies are designed, manufactured, used and disposed of.

questions.q: Which example of a positive societal impact does the framework give?
options: Chatbots in public sector call centres cutting costs and speeding up cases
questions.explain: The same changes also raise questions about effects on people.
questions.evidence: adopting chatbots in public sector call centres might reduce costs, boost productivity and allow for faster handling of cases

questions.q: What can the context and mechanisms of data collection affect?
options: Who is, and is not, represented in a dataset
questions.explain: Under-represented groups can be badly served by the resulting systems.
questions.evidence: the context and mechanisms of data collection can have a significant impact on who is, and is not, represented in a data set

questions.q: To understand how data and AI affect society, what do you need to understand?
options: The broader social and technical context they are used and built in
questions.explain: Impacts depend on where and how a system is deployed.
questions.evidence: you need to understand the broader social and technical context in which they are used and built

questions.q: Which harms linked to technology supply chains does the framework mention?
options: Displacement of local communities and food and water scarcity
questions.explain: These fall hardest on already vulnerable parts of the world.
questions.evidence: This includes the displacement of local communities, and food and water scarcity in already vulnerable parts of the world.
